channel.title: The shad0w blog
channel.description: System Zero, certified LLM shortcuts, and shad0w in production.

item.title: Adding a category without breaking production
item.description: A trained shortcut and a changing list of options are a dangerous mix. What goes wrong, the rule shad0w follows now, and the lifecycle of an option from rename to retirement.

item.title: System Zero: the reflex layer your LLM stack is missing
item.description: LLMs think slowly. Decision models think fast. But most of what an app asks is a repeat, and repeats need a reflex. A case for System Zero, and how shad0w implements it.

item.title: How can a small table promise it agrees with your LLM?
item.description: The certificate behind shad0w, in plain words: a held-out test, a confidence line, an allowance for bad luck, and what the promise does and does not cover.

item.title: What we measured: where shad0w wins, and where it loses
item.description: Real LLMs, real proxies, public datasets and the same certifier for every method. The numbers that make shad0w worth using, and the ones that show when not to.
